beats.text: Five things your body says about you before you open your mouth.
One. Eye contact. Steady and warm reads as confidence; darting reads as fear.
Two. Posture. An open chest and squared shoulders say 'I belong here.' Hunching says the opposite.
Three. Hands. Visible, relaxed hands build trust. Hidden hands quietly read as hiding something.
Four. Feet. They tend to point toward whatever — or whoever — truly has your attention.
Five. The smile. A real one crinkles the eyes. A polite one stops at the mouth, and people feel it.
You're always communicating. The only question is whether your body agrees with your words.
